meta.protocol: streaming /v1/completions, usage.completion_tokens counted, temp 0, ignore_eos, warmup 1 + 3 samples
meta.purpose: Ninfer trick A/B: lm-head-draft (MTP_DRAFT_VOCAB=0) and fp8-KV long context

A.config: dflash2 k=7 CTX=fast bf16 64k, MAX_SEQS=1, GPU_UTIL=0.90, KV unpinned

B.config: mtp k=4 CTX=fast bf16 64k (truncated 40k draft head), MAX_SEQS=1, GPU_UTIL=0.90

C.config: mtp k=4 CTX=fast MTP_DRAFT_VOCAB=0 (full 248k shared lm_head drafting = Ninfer --lm-head-draft)

D.config: dflash2 k=7 CTX=long fp8 KV 131072 ctx (host-KV capability analogue), MAX_SEQS=1, GPU_UTIL=0.90, KV unpinned

conclusions.lm_head_draft: HURTS: C vs B decode256 119.2 vs 133.1 tok/s (-10.4%), decode900 113.1 vs 119.8 (-5.6%). The truncated 40k draft head is the right design on this stack; the wider acceptance of the full 248k head does not pay for the 6x wider draft GEMM.
conclusions.fp8_kv_long: Costs 3.4% decode256 vs bf16 fast (135.8 vs 140.5) and 19.5% prefill (1741 vs 2161), buys 131k context on a single card. Host-KV offload itself is unnecessary at 64GB VRAM.
conclusions.node_variance: Boot A re-measured the v9 config at 140.5 vs 147.7 tok/s on a different physical card; same config, same protocol. Treat ~5% as cross-node spread.

acceptance_metrics_note: Server-side SpecDecoding metrics from the final log: boot B/C mean acceptance 2.38-2.52 (k=4, mtp), boot D mean acceptance 2.49-2.61 (k=7, dflash2).
